description: This file contains an abstract class RestSerializer responsible for serializing HTTP requests in AWS SDK, handling different parts like headers, query parameters, request URI, payload, and body for RESTful API interactions. It is used as a base class for specific REST serializers within the AWS SDK for PHP.

classes.name: RestSerializer
classes.description: Abstract base class for serializing HTTP requests in AWS SDK, handling location-based serialization of request components such as headers, query parameters, URI, and payload.

methods.name: __construct
methods.description: Initializes the serializer with the AWS service description and endpoint URI.

methods.name: __invoke
methods.description: Main method to serialize a command into an HTTP Request object, resolving endpoint and applying parameter location logic.

methods.name: payload
methods.description: Abstract method to serialize the payload part of the request; to be implemented by subclasses.

methods.name: serialize
methods.description: Serializes operation input parameters into request options, including headers, query, and payload.

methods.name: applyPayload
methods.description: Handles serialization of payload or streaming bodies.

methods.name: applyHeader
methods.description: Serializes a header value with proper formatting based on its type.

methods.name: applyHeaderMap
methods.description: Serializes a map of headers, used especially for service-specific headers.

methods.name: buildEndpoint
methods.description: Constructs the endpoint URI, replacing URI template variables with actual values from the input.

methods.name: hasPayloadParam
methods.description: Checks whether the input structure has a payload member that should be serialized.

methods.name: appendQuery
methods.description: Helper to append query parameters to the endpoint URI.

methods.name: getVarDefinitions
methods.description: Extracts variable definitions for URI path expansion from command input members.

methods.name: normalizePath
methods.description: Ensures the URI path has a trailing slash if needed.
